normalized.description:
Open Research Europe (ORE) is the open access peer-reviewed publishing platform offered by the Commission as an optional service to Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe beneficiaries at no cost to them. It was launched in March 2021 and currently has approximately 500 publications and 900 peer-reviews. ORE follows an innovative open access publishing model for articles, which is based on open peer-review after publication (post-publication peer-review). 
The Commission’s vision, in collaboration with a number of national funders, is that as of 2026 ORE will transition from a publishing platform for Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe beneficiaries into a publishing platform for which responsibility could be shared with Member State funders and possibly also research performing organisations.
The Commission is herewith tendering the open source publishing platform that will underpin ORE as of 2026, which will be largely based on existing open source software for scientific publishing.

normalized.description: The Green Municipalities II Project aims to improve the climate efficiency of Algerian local authorities, with a particular focus on reducing energy consumption, greenhouse gas emissions and energy-related costs, while improving the quality and sustainability of municipal services. The project supports Algerian local authorities in strengthening their technical, institutional and operational capacities in the fields of municipal energy management, energy efficiency, renewable energy and sustainable urban services. It combines capacity building, technical assistance, digital tools and the implementation of practical pilot measures to enable municipalities to improve their energy performance and adopt more sustainable management practices. Particular attention is given to the main energy-consuming sectors within municipalities, including public lighting, schools, mosques, administrative buildings, green spaces and other public facilities. The project supports local authorities in identifying, planning, implementing and monitoring practical solutions in energy efficiency and renewable energy, while promoting digital technologies and smart management tools. The project is implemented with a strong focus on pilot municipalities and wilayas in order to develop practical, scalable and replicable solutions. The experience gained through these pilot interventions will contribute to strengthening the capacities of local stakeholders and to developing models that can subsequently be replicated in other Algerian municipalities. The project targets, among other objectives, the strengthening of the capacities of technical staff responsible for energy management, the use of digital tools for municipal energy management, the implementation of priority measures identified through municipal action plans, and the development of citizen participation in measures aimed at improving municipal climate efficiency. Overall, Green Municipalities II seeks to establish the technical, institutional and operational conditions for Algerian local authorities to manage their energy resources and urban services in a more efficient, sustainable and data-driven manner.

normalized.description: SKDP is seeking to deliver an environmental educational short course which is both informative and practical and which will be made available for participation to the public in the South Kerry area. This initiative is being developed in line with the 2023 – 2027 LEADER programme objectives which incorporates a number of thematic areas, one of which is ‘Sustainable Development and Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation’. A sub-theme under this core theme is ‘Climate Change Capacity Building’. Climate change presents an ever-growing and existential challenge to Kerry’s rich and biodiverse ecological habitats and overall environmental health. This challenge is one which will affect not only our natural flora and fauna but also the wellness and health of our communities as well as their economic resilience as Kerry’s economy is heavily reliant on tourism. The Kerry Local Development Strategy which was developed through public participation to inform the core objectives of this current iteration of LEADER, found that an understanding of the science of climate change and in particular how Ireland and Southwest Ireland will be affected was a noticeable knowledge gap when engaging with the local communities. Priorities identified under the current LEADER programme include the provision of environmental educational training resources. To identify the specific areas of environmental education which groups would be most interested in, SKDP undertook a short public survey which was widely distributed to communities and community groups and remained open for 4.5 weeks. SKDP received 49 responses, with the outcome directing this RFT. SKDP are now seeking to enlist the expertise of an experienced environmental education/ training provider to develop and deliver an environmental education course. It is envisaged that this course will support the needs and priorities of these groups and their communities and support them to take meaningful local action for the environment. The objective of this RFT is to seek tenders from environmental education / training providers for the delivery of an environmental education course which will support communities to take meaningful local action to support biodiversity and to increase the resilience of habitats in their local areas. The course should be delivered as three modules. This is to enable participants, if they are unable to complete the full course, to complete one or two modules. The modules are as follows: 1. Seed Saving, Pollinators and Meadow Management 2. Tree Planting and Long-Term Management 3. Invasive Species Identification and Management The below are suggested inclusions for each module.
